subject: physics
title: Required practical: force, mass and acceleration
key_idea: Investigate how acceleration depends on force and on mass using a trolley. Keep the total mass constant when changing the force. Compensate for friction. Measure acceleration with light gates, or from distance and time.

blocks.text: This practical shows how the acceleration of an object depends on the resultant force on it and on its mass. There are two investigations.

items.meaning: The trolley plus the weight hanger and masses attached to it.
Tilting the runway so friction is balanced and the trolley rolls at a constant speed.

items: Investigation 1 varies force and keeps mass constant.
Investigation 2 varies mass and keeps force constant.

blocks.text: A trolley is pulled along a runway by a weight hanger. The weights on the hanger provide the force.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for investigating force and acceleration in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the steps of the force and acceleration investigation in order.
steps: Set up a trolley on a runway, joined by a string over a pulley to a weight hanger.
Raise one end of the runway until the trolley rolls at a constant speed, to compensate for friction.
Put all the slotted masses on the trolley, so the total mass is fixed.
Move one mass at a time from the trolley to the hanger to increase the force.
Release the trolley and use light gates to measure its acceleration.
Plot a graph of acceleration against force.

items: Transfer mass between the trolley and the hanger.
Mass removed from the trolley equals mass added to the hanger, so the total mass does not change.
The force comes from the weight of the masses on the hanger.

blocks.label: Weight
where: g: gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram, N/kg

items: Keep the same mass on the hanger, so the force is constant.
Add masses to the trolley, one at a time.
Compensate for friction by tilting the runway until the trolley rolls at a constant speed.
Move masses between trolley and hanger to keep the total mass constant.
Use light gates, or timing and a ruler, to find the acceleration.

blocks.text: Light gates and a computer can give the acceleration directly. Without them, use distance and time.

blocks.label: Average acceleration
where: a: acceleration in metres per second squared, m/s²
Δv: change in velocity in metres per second, m/s
t: time taken in seconds, s

items: For a trolley released from rest with constant acceleration, divide distance by time to get the mean speed.
Double the mean speed to get the final speed.
Divide the final speed by the time to get the acceleration.

diagram.alt: Calculate the acceleration of a trolley from the distance and time of its run.
diagram.question: A trolley is released from rest. It moves {s} m in {t} s with constant acceleration. Calculate its acceleration.

items: With constant mass, acceleration is proportional to resultant force: the graph is a straight line through the origin.
With constant force, acceleration decreases as mass increases.
The acceleration comes from the change in velocity divided by the time taken.
Acceleration is proportional to force when mass is constant.
Acceleration decreases as mass increases when force is constant.

checks.q: State the independent variable and the control variable when investigating how force affects acceleration.
checks.a: The independent variable is the resultant force. The control variable is the mass of the moving system.

checks.q: How can the student keep the total mass constant while the force changes?
checks.a: Transfer masses between the trolley and the weight hanger.

checks.q: Explain how the student can compensate for friction on the runway.
checks.a: Raise one end of the runway until the trolley, not attached to the hanger, rolls at a constant speed.

exam_phrases: divide distance travelled by time taken to give (average / mean) velocity
double mean velocity (to give maximum velocity)
divide change in velocity by time taken (to give acceleration)
use light gate(s) to determine time and / or speed
attach a mass holder to the string
repeat for different numbers of slotted masses

mistakes.wrong: The distance divided by the time is the acceleration.
mistakes.right: Distance ÷ time gives the average velocity. Double it, then divide the change in velocity by the time.

mistakes.wrong: I will do one reading with one mass on the holder.
mistakes.right: Repeat for different numbers of slotted masses, so you can see how acceleration changes with force.

mistakes.wrong: I will just describe the trolley and a stopclock.
mistakes.right: Name the extra equipment: a pulley, a string, a mass holder and slotted masses, and light gates or a metre rule and timer.

worked_example.question:
The student held the trolley stationary and then released it. The trolley moved along the runway with a constant acceleration.
The student recorded the time taken for the trolley to travel a measured distance along the runway.
For one set of results, the force acting through the string was 2.0 N.

Describe how the acceleration of the trolley can be calculated using the time taken and distance travelled by the trolley.
answer_points: Divide the distance travelled by the time taken to give the average (mean) velocity
Double the mean velocity to give the maximum velocity
Divide the change in velocity by the time taken to give the acceleration
worked_example.tip: Speed can be used instead of velocity throughout. Using v² = u² + 2as is also allowed.

exam_phrases: raise one end of the runway
(force of) gravity (on the trolley) balances forces of friction
transfer mass between trolley and hanger
add weight / mass to the weight hanger
keeping mass constant by moving weights between hanger and trolley

mistakes.wrong: To keep the mass constant, I add more weights to the hanger.
mistakes.right: Transfer mass between the trolley and the hanger, so the total mass does not change.

mistakes.wrong: Friction is the same each time, so I can ignore it.
mistakes.right: Compensate for friction. Raise one end of the runway so the trolley rolls at a constant speed.

mistakes.wrong: I increase the force by adding weights to the trolley.
mistakes.right: Add weight to the weight hanger to increase the accelerating force.

worked_example.question:
A student investigates the relationship between force and acceleration for a trolley on a runway. A weight hanger on a string pulls the trolley.

Explain how the student could improve the procedure to compensate for the effects of frictional forces acting on the trolley.
answer_points: Raise one end of the runway
So that the trolley (not attached to the weight hanger) rolls at a constant speed, or just starts to move
The force of gravity on the trolley balances the forces of friction
worked_example.tip: One mark for raising one end of the runway and one for the reason. Methods that reduce friction directly, such as oiling the wheels, are also credited.
